correctness.rationale: The boundary Jacobian is triangular, with transverse entry cx; tangent–transverse mixing does not change the product of the transverse diagonal entries. Under x=4 sin²(πθ), the starting law is the stated arcsine law and evolution is a factor of angle doubling. For X=2−2 cos(2πθ) the invariant-measure transfer operator P gives PX=2. For Rf=P(X²f), R1=6+2C and RC=−4−4C with C=cos(2πθ), by keeping only the even cosines before halving frequencies. The trace 2 and determinant −16 and initial moments 1 and 6 give the recurrence, two-root formula, and positive relative variance exponent. As a fresh check, writing the product as the squared modulus of the finite Thue–Morse polynomial, the sum of squared finite aperiodic autocorrelations gave 6,28,152,752,3936,19904,102784 for n=1,…,7 and the coefficient-square sums gave 2^n. Log X is in L² with mean zero and cosine coefficients −2/k, so matching frequencies under doubling gives covariance π²/(3·2^m). Counting lag pairs gives the finite variance. The reverse martingale difference d=2φ−φ∘D has Pd=0, variance π², and the sum differs from Z_n by a uniformly L²-bounded endpoint term; the ergodic reverse martingale CLT applies. Birkhoff gives the almost-sure exponential rate; the CLT and the shift n log c_n=κ√n give Φ(κ/π). These are claims about a linearized boundary cocycle, not finite-density invasion. The frozen code was inspected but not executed.
residual_risks: Excluding zero-measure singular orbits suffices for the logarithmic steps. The finite exact calculations do not establish the CLT or its hypotheses.

evidence: From Eq. (A35) set Q_p f(t)=t^p[f(t_+)+f(t_−)]/2. The finite normalized raw moment is ∫Q_p^n 1 dμ, by transfer and stationarity (postweight uses t_1,…,t_n, equivalent in law to t_0,…,t_(n−1)). For p=1 the initial image is t, with Q_1 t=t/2; the arcsine first moment is 1/2. For p=2 the initial image is t². The two inverse branches sum to 1 and multiply to t/4; thus on (t²,t³) the matrix has first column (1/2,−1/4) and second column (1/2,−3/8). Its trace and determinant are 1/8 and −1/16. Cayley–Hamilton, scaled by 16^n, gives u_(n+2)=2u_(n+1)+16u_n for n≥1; the initial arcsine integrals give u_0=1, u_1=6, u_2=28, also establishing the n=0 step.
Eq. (A32) plus lag pair-counting gives Var(Z_n)=(π²/3)(3n−4+2^(2−n)). Center the prior sum by n log 4, apply the CLT (variance π²), then shift the normal threshold by κ.

originality.rationale: Defaveri–Smith give both the exact logarithmic covariance at every lag and the polynomial tilted operator for the same arcsine logistic orbit. Their stated eigenvalue alone would not fix the finite prefactor, but their explicit operator and invariant polynomial span mechanically give the full first and second moments, not just their leading rates. Stationary lag counting and a threshold shift of the known CLT then cover the other quantitative claims. The new transverse label does not change this calculation.
residual_risks: No claim is made about who first wrote the exact recurrence in this normalization. The known exact operator and covariance are enough for the coverage verdict without needing an earlier match for every displayed number.

value.rationale: The annealed versus quenched distinction is a meaningful way to interpret transverse neutrality, but here the predator-free derivative simply multiplies the same logistic observable already examined in the prior work. Both moment rates and every finite-horizon law claimed here follow from its exact calculations or the known limit theorem. No independent nonlinear invasion statement, new observable, or surviving exact invariant is established, so the interpretation alone does not repair the claim.
residual_risks: The formulas can still help explain this example; no conclusion about nonlinear persistence or broader transverse dynamics was reviewed.
